First listed: 2025-07-18 | Evaluation cutoff: 2026-11-10

## Source versions

- [YouTube: Earnings Season Kickoff, Bank Earnings & Nvidia China Greenlight - The Friday Market Wrap!](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PZUMfLcOyYk) - 2025-07-18
- [Substack: Earnings Season Kickoff, Bank Earnings & Nvidia China Greenlight - The Friday Market Wrap!](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/earnings-season-kickoff-bank-earnings-467) - 2025-07-19

Earliest listed publication among matched versions, not proof of an unedited contemporaneous archive. Claim timestamps refer to the reviewed version.

## Summary

Eisman uses the first earnings week to demonstrate thesis checking and bank valuation. He compares tangible-equity returns across major banks, distinguishes earnings beats from stock reactions, and explains his move from GFC bearishness to a predominantly long US portfolio. Corporate observations are contemporaneous diagnoses, not newly successful forecasts.

His best contribution is relating bank profitability to valuation while explicitly acknowledging exceptions. The stronger claims about permanent safety, unique US technology exposure and Citi never recovering an old price are not precise, finite predictions. Earnings-season evidence supports resilience but does not make tariffs the only possible risk.

## Material claims

<a id="youtube-PZUMfLcOyYk-c001"></a>
### 001. Allowing Nvidia H20 exports signals a more selective China technology policy.

**Unresolved** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 2:26-3:04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PZUMfLcOyYk&t=146s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

A license decision can change while other controls persist. One product exception does not establish a durable policy regime.

Assessment test: Track actual licenses, shipments and the broader export-control schedule.


<a id="youtube-PZUMfLcOyYk-c002"></a>
### 002. Strong earnings do not guarantee a positive immediate stock reaction because expectations and positioning matter.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | analytical principle | major

[Source at 3:15-4:06](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PZUMfLcOyYk&t=195s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

Price reflects expected future cash flows and risk, not only the reported growth rate. A positive result can still fall short of expectations.

Conditional reasoning: If investors expected a larger increase in future cash flows than the announcement supports, the estimate of value can fall even when reported earnings rise.

Assessment test: Compare results with dated expectations and changes in forward estimates.


<a id="youtube-PZUMfLcOyYk-c003"></a>
### 003. Higher sustainable tangible-equity returns generally justify a higher tangible-book multiple.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | analytical principle | major

[Source at 4:06-5:17](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PZUMfLcOyYk&t=246s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

A residual-income model links value above book to future returns exceeding the required return, holding risk and growth assumptions comparable. The observed relationship need not be exact.

Conditional reasoning: Value equals book plus the discounted value of future income above the equity charge. Higher sustainable return on the same equity base raises residual income and justified price/book.

Assessment test: Compare normalized returns, cost of equity, growth and capital requirements.


<a id="youtube-PZUMfLcOyYk-c004"></a>
### 004. JPMorgan combines high tangible-equity profitability with strong trading and investment banking.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 5:17-6:02](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PZUMfLcOyYk&t=317s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The dated issuer report supports the operating description. Best in the business is read relative to the named large-bank peer group, not every financial institution worldwide.

Assessment test: Compare consistently defined returns and revenue by business.

- [JPMorgan Q2 2025 results](https://www.jpmorganchase.com/content/dam/jpmc/jpmorgan-chase-and-co/investor-relations/documents/quarterly-earnings/2025/2nd-quarter/ac5b7d95-9133-4fea-959c-2fa6d8fd8c5b.pdf) (2025-07-15): Reported ROTCE was 21%, with strong markets revenue. This is a dated profitability observation, not a stock-return forecast.

<a id="youtube-PZUMfLcOyYk-c005"></a>
### 005. The Wells Fargo asset cap constrained growth and its removal will not produce an immediate smooth recovery.

**Mixed** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 6:02-7:46](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PZUMfLcOyYk&t=362s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The cap and uneven net-interest performance are real. Attributing the entire NII shortfall to the cap is too strong because rates, deposit mix and other balance-sheet choices also matter.

Assessment test: Separate cap restrictions from pricing, funding and reserve-release effects.

- [Wells Fargo Q2 2025 results](https://www.wellsfargo.com/assets/pdf/about/investor-relations/earnings/second-quarter-2025-financial-results.pdf) (2025-07-15): The bank reported 15.2% ROTCE and weaker year-over-year net interest income. Rate, deposit and balance-sheet mix effects accompany the legacy asset-cap constraint.
- [Wells Fargo asset-growth restriction removed](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/enforcement20250603a.htm) (2025-06-03): The Fed removed the asset-growth restriction after required remediation. Other provisions of the enforcement action remained in place.

<a id="youtube-PZUMfLcOyYk-c006"></a>
### 006. Citi is improving but its low ROTCE explains a valuation discount to stronger peers.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 7:46-9:13](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PZUMfLcOyYk&t=466s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The 8.7% return and improving revenue support the profitability comparison. Risk, growth and restructuring credibility also affect the multiple.

- [Citi Q2 2025 results](https://www.citigroup.com/rcs/citigpa/storage/public/2025prqtr2rslt.pdf) (2025-07-15): Reported ROTCE was 8.7%; revenue grew 8%. Improving operations did not yet produce peer-leading profitability.

<a id="youtube-PZUMfLcOyYk-c007"></a>
### 007. Citi will never again reach its split-adjusted pre-crisis stock-price peak.

**Not testable** | Steve Eisman | forecast | major

[Source at 9:13-9:45](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PZUMfLcOyYk&t=553s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

Never has no finite verification date, and nominal prices can change with future splits and inflation. Past dilution does not mathematically impose a permanent price ceiling.

Assessment test: Use an explicit horizon and split-adjusted total-return benchmark.

<a id="youtube-PZUMfLcOyYk-c012"></a>
### 012. Bank of America legacy low-yield bond purchases constrain its earnings and tangible-equity returns.

**Mixed** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 12:54-14:05](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PZUMfLcOyYk&t=774s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

Low-yield assets can depress relative earnings, and the reported return was 13.4%. Yet NII was already growing; unrealized losses are not themselves the full explanation of a revenue miss.

Assessment test: Decompose asset yields, deposit costs, balances and securities maturities.

- [Bank of America Q2 2025 presentation](https://investor.bankofamerica.com/regulatory-and-other-filings/select-sec-filings/content/0000070858-25-000254/bac063025ex992.htm) (2025-07-16): ROTCE was 13.4%. Net interest income rose from the preceding quarter and year; low-yielding legacy assets were not equivalent to an immediate insolvency conclusion.

<a id="youtube-PZUMfLcOyYk-c013"></a>
### 013. Valuation anomalies can reflect expectations for future normalization rather than current-quarter returns.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | analytical principle | major

[Source at 14:05-15:45](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PZUMfLcOyYk&t=845s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

A valuation model depends on future income rather than a mechanical capitalization of one quarter. The specific motives of marginal investors remain unobserved.

Conditional reasoning: Two firms with equal current earnings can have different value if expected growth, risk or future margins differ. Current-quarter ROTCE alone cannot determine the price/book multiple.

Assessment test: Compare implied future returns with analyst and management forecasts.

## Framework and tools

- Use earnings to test a thesis rather than guess the next trading-day reaction.
- Compare sustainable ROTCE with price to tangible book, then explain exceptions.
- Separate recurring income from reserve releases and investment gains.
- Update a market stance when bank leverage and the opportunity set change.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- Annualized ROTCE
- Price to tangible book value
- Net interest income and margin
- Loan-loss provisions and reserve releases
- Trading and advisory revenue
- Long-term asset-manager flows
- Medical loss trends
- Sector weights including reclassified technology businesses

## Source cautions

Steve Eisman presents; speaker attribution follows the full dialogue.
- Reported and adjusted earnings are mixed in the narration; the audit uses each issuer definition.
- The narrated bank table is discussed as a tool, not claimed as an independently captured chart.
- Personal medical details are outside the material investment-claim scope.
